title: Monotheism
english: We offer hymns of gratitude to the one who is, and there is no other, for He is the one who made heaven and earth, and did not make it in vain, but for habitation.

If He is the creator of heaven and earth, who else could be thought of as God besides Him, or who could be equal to Him in power and glory, since the nature of created things is inferior to such great and surpassing glory, strength, and wisdom?

Thus, there is no one else like Him, and only He is God by nature and truth, and He is the Lord of all, speaking righteousness and proclaiming truth many times, and not just once, but repeatedly, many times.
But someone might ask, who knows His purpose, or who can say whether He wants to crown others with His glory and calling, or only Himself?
He apologizes and says, I did not speak in secret, nor in a dark place, but clearly and openly, for I did not say to the seed of Jacob, seek empty things.

Instead, I gave laws concerning these things, not speaking in a whisper, nor trying to hide, for the Lord came down on Mount Sinai in the form of fire, and there was a cloud and a storm and smoke, and the sound of a trumpet, as all the people stood near, with Moses mediating, and the laws were proclaimed by God.

The laws proclaimed by God did not encourage Israel to seek empty things, that is, idols, or false worship, but rather, they were commands that kept them away from such things, as it is said, you shall worship the Lord your God, and serve Him only, and you shall have no other gods besides Me (Exodus 20:3).
Additionally, it is written, you shall not make an idol for yourself, nor any likeness of what is in heaven above, or on earth below, or in the waters under the earth (Exodus 20:4).

This statement is reminiscent of God's declaration, 'I am the Lord,' which is similar to saying, 'I am God alone,' and 'I am the Lord of all,' speaking righteousness and proclaiming truth many times, and not just once.
When God speaks of righteousness, He is referring to the law, for the law is the awarder of righteousness, the standard by which righteousness is measured.
Truth, however, is revealed through the teachings of Christ, and the law contains the formation of truth, and the mystery of Christ is hidden in the shadows, although Moses wrote about Him.
However, when righteousness is spoken, the power of truth is also proclaimed, since the law was only a shadow of the truth, but now the formation of truth is revealed.
The dragon, the apostate, has led those on earth away from their relationship with God.
It is time for those who are saved from the nations to gather together and reason with one another (Isaiah 45:20).
The woodcarvers do not know the wood they carve, and they pray to them as gods, which do not save.

title: God's Sovereignty
english: If God desires to act, what could possibly hinder Him, and who could stand to resist Him? For who would dare to scatter that which the holy God intends? And whose hand could ever turn back His high hand? Therefore, to demonstrate that God is truly and by nature so, it is reasonably said of Him, 'All my counsel will stand, and all that I have purposed, I will do' (Isaiah 46:10). Then He declares, 'I will call a bird from the east, and from a far-off land, concerning what I have purposed' (Isaiah 46:11). And the consequence follows, 'I am.'

This bird, called from the east and from a far-off land, is the Babylonian, who laid waste to the whole land of the Jews, seized Jerusalem, and destroyed the temple. Having raised up many among both the common people and the prominent, he led them away, and once he had taken them, he imposed upon them a harsh and unbearable yoke of captivity. This will become clear to you through what God spoke to the blessed prophet Ezekiel.

The great eagle with long wings of great extension and full of claws, whose narrative involves entering Lebanon, took the choice parts of the cedar, the topmost tender shoots, and brought them to the land of Canaan to a fortified city; he took from the seed of the land and planted it in the plain amidst much water, setting it under care, until it became a weak vine, small in size, with its branches upon it and its roots beneath the ground. It became a vine that produced fruit and spread out its branches. God spoke these things to the prophet Ezekiel.

Because the word was difficult to understand and the power of the thoughts was not very clear to those listening, he himself interprets it once more, saying: 'I spoke to the rebellious house of Israel, yet you do not know what these things are that I have said.' When the king of Babylon comes to Jerusalem, he takes its king and its leaders and brings them to Babylon.

He will take from the seed of the kingdom, making a covenant with him and bringing him into an oath, and he will take the leaders of the land to establish a weak kingdom, so that they shall not exalt themselves to keep his covenant and establish it.

title: Divine Patience and Human Stubbornness
english: It became audible to you, and I made it happen suddenly, and it came upon you; that is to say, even if you did not expect it to reach its end, you nonetheless came to know through their experiences and their trials that I made it and it came upon you.

It seems he is speaking earlier of the affliction brought upon them from the war, when those who carried them away had become exhausted and had taken on the yoke of bitter servitude, being led away into the land of the Persians and Medes.
Second, after these things, what was brought upon the Babylonians from divine wrath has happened, which has already been told to us in many words.
I know that you are hard, and your neck is an iron sinew, and your forehead is bronze.
And I announced to you long ago before you came upon me, I made it audible to you.
These things demonstrate the unchangeable gentleness of the highest nature, and how much toward humans it exercises mercy, and if anyone were among those accustomed to bring him down.
For it holds its serenity equal to its own glory.
And just as the measure of the things that are born exceeds excess, so it is also incomparably loving toward humanity.
Let him see how, even though knowing Israel to be hard, having a forehead of brass and an unyielding neck, so that also …
